1: // Package router decides where a request should be executed: local Ollama,
2: // frontier API, or both (fusion). Routing is two-tier: a cheap regex DSL
3: // fast-pass that handles obvious cases, and an SLM fallback that asks a
4: // small local model to judge complexity when the DSL has no opinion.
5: package router
6: 
7: import (
8: 	"fmt"
9: 	"log"
10: 	"regexp"
11: 	"strings"
12: 	"unicode"
13: 
14: 	"github.com/anchapin/nexus-proxy/internal/telemetry"
15: )
16: 
17: // Route names are the canonical string identifiers used across packages.
18: const (
19: 	RouteLocal    = "local"
20: 	RouteFrontier = "frontier"
21: 	RouteFusion   = "fusion"
22: )
23: 
24: // Default DSL patterns. These match the hardcoded behaviour prior to issue #305.
25: // Exported so the chat handler can fall back to them when the config fields
26: // are nil (e.g. in tests that construct config.Config directly).
27: //
28: // The patterns are compiled via mustCompileDefaultPattern (issue #588) so that
29: // an invalid default surfaces as a structured boot error (log.Fatalf) rather
30: // than a runtime panic from regexp.MustCompile.
31: var (
32: 	DefaultFormattingPatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{
33: 		mustCompileDefaultPattern("formatting", `(?i)\b(css|format|docstring|lint|typo|boilerplate|debug|fix bug|git commit|sql query|parse json|validate input|regex|api endpoint|test|optimize|readme)\b`),
34: 	}
35: 	DefaultFusionPatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{
36: 		mustCompileDefaultPattern("fusion", `(?i)\b(architectural design|system architecture)\b`),
37: 	}
38: 	DefaultLocalPatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{
39: 		mustCompileDefaultPattern("local", `(?i)\b(refactor|security scan|generate tests|explain this code|performance analysis)\b`),
40: 	}
41: 	// DefaultUnicodePatterns matches non-ASCII text categories (issue #422).
42: 	// Operators can override via NEXUS_DSL_UNICODE_PATTERNS.
43: 	DefaultUnicodePatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{
44: 		mustCompileDefaultPattern("unicode", `(?i)\p{Han}`),    // Chinese characters
45: 		mustCompileDefaultPattern("unicode", `(?i)\p{Arabic}`), // Arabic characters
46: 	}
47: )

49: // compileDefaultPattern compiles a single default DSL regex expression and
50: // returns a descriptive error identifying the pattern group (formatting,
51: // fusion, local, or unicode) if the syntax is invalid. It never panics.
52: // This is the testable core of mustCompileDefaultPattern (issue #588).
53: func compileDefaultPattern(name, expr string) (*regexp.Regexp, error) {
54: 	re, err := regexp.Compile(expr)
55: 	if err != nil {
56: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("dsl: invalid default %s pattern %q: %w", name, expr, err)
57: 	}
58: 	return re, nil
59: }

61: // mustCompileDefaultPattern compiles a default DSL regex expression and is
62: // intended for package-level var initialization. On invalid syntax it logs a
63: // descriptive message (identifying the pattern group and the parse error) and
64: // calls log.Fatalf, so the proxy exits with a clear boot error instead of a
65: // panic (issue #588).
66: func mustCompileDefaultPattern(name, expr string) *regexp.Regexp {
67: 	re, err := compileDefaultPattern(name, expr)
68: 	if err != nil {
69: 		log.Fatalf("%v", err)

71: 	return re

74: // Guardrail returns RouteFrontier when the prompt is too large for the
75: // configured VRAM budget. The threshold is the maximum *estimated* token
76: // count the local model can safely handle. When maxTokens <= 0 the
77: // guardrail is disabled and ("", false) is returned.
78: func Guardrail(prompt string, maxTokens int) (Route, bool) {
79: 	if maxTokens <= 0 {
80: 		return "", false
81: 	}
82: 	if telemetry.EstimateTokens(prompt) > maxTokens {
83: 		return RouteFrontier, true
84: 	}
85: 	return "", false

88: // Route is a string alias for the routing decision. Use the Route* constants
89: // rather than raw strings so typos surface at compile time.
90: type Route string

92: // DSL runs the heuristic fast-pass. Returns one of RouteLocal, RouteFusion,
93: // or "" if no rule matched (caller should fall back to the SLM).
94: //
95: // fusionPatterns matches architecture keywords that warrant fusion (both
96: // local and frontier). formattingPatterns matches simple formatting keywords
97: // (css, format, docstring, lint, typo, boilerplate). localPatterns matches
98: // common coding task keywords (refactor, security scan, generate tests,
99: // explain this code, performance analysis, etc.). unicodePatterns matches
100: // non-ASCII text categories (e.g. Chinese characters via \p{Han}) via
101: // NEXUS_DSL_UNICODE_PATTERNS (issue #422). Each pattern slice may be
102: // nil or empty in which case that branch is skipped.
103: func DSL(prompt string, fusionPatterns, formattingPatterns, localPatterns, unicodePatterns []*regexp.Regexp) (Route, bool) {
104: 	lower := toUnicodeLower(prompt)
105: 
106: 	if len(fusionPatterns) > 0 {
107: 		for _, re := range fusionPatterns {
108: 			if re.MatchString(lower) {
109: 				return RouteFusion, true
110: 			}
111: 		}
112: 	}
113: 	if len(formattingPatterns) > 0 {
114: 		for _, re := range formattingPatterns {
115: 			if re.MatchString(lower) {
116: 				return RouteLocal, true
117: 			}
118: 		}
119: 	}
120: 	if len(localPatterns) > 0 {
121: 		for _, re := range localPatterns {
122: 			if re.MatchString(lower) {
123: 				return RouteLocal, true
124: 			}
125: 		}
126: 	}
127: 	// Unicode patterns match non-ASCII text directly (issue #422).
128: 	// These patterns are NOT lowercased because they target script
129: 	// categories (e.g. \p{Han}) rather than ASCII keywords.
130: 	if len(unicodePatterns) > 0 {
131: 		for _, re := range unicodePatterns {
132: 			if re.MatchString(prompt) {
133: 				return RouteLocal, true
134: 			}
135: 		}
136: 	}
137: 	return "", false
138: }
139: 
140: // toUnicodeLower converts s to lowercase using Unicode case-folding rules
141: // (issue #422). Unlike the prior toLowerASCII, this handles all scripts
142: // (Chinese, Arabic, Greek, etc.). The allocation is proportional to the
143: // number of uppercase runes in s; prompts without uppercase return s
144: // unchanged (zero allocation).
145: func toUnicodeLower(s string) string {
146: 	if !hasUpperUnicode(s) {
147: 		return s
148: 	}
149: 	var b strings.Builder
150: 	b.Grow(len(s))
151: 	for _, r := range s {
152: 		b.WriteRune(unicode.ToLower(r))
153: 	}
154: 	return b.String()
155: }
156: 
157: // hasUpperUnicode returns true if s contains any uppercase Unicode rune.
158: // Used to skip the toUnicodeLower allocation for already-lowercase strings.
159: func hasUpperUnicode(s string) bool {
160: 	for _, r := range s {
161: 		if r != unicode.ToLower(r) {
162: 			return true
163: 		}
164: 	}
165: 	return false
166: }
167: 
168: func stringsContains(s, substr string) bool {
169: 	return len(substr) == 0 || (len(s) >= len(substr) && indexOf(s, substr) >= 0)
170: }
171: 
172: func indexOf(s, substr string) int {
173: 	n, m := len(s), len(substr)
174: 	for i := 0; i+m <= n; i++ {
175: 		if s[i:i+m] == substr {
176: 			return i
177: 		}
178: 	}
179: 	return -1
180: }
